data.title: Wall Street soars on Huang's return to Nvidia, Treasury yields rise
data.description:
Key points:
  • Nvidia shares surge 31% on Jensen Huang's return
  • Dollar index hits 19-month high with bets on a hawkish Fed
  • Tech shares lead indexes higher, S&P gains 4.7%

By Sabrina Valle

US stocks soared on Monday after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive following pressure from US President Donald Trump. Shorter-dated US Treasury yields climbed and the dollar rose as traders bet on a more hawkish Federal Reserve.

The company's decision sparked a sharp reversal of last week's global equity market rout, triggered in part by the leadership crisis at the chipmaker. Nvidia shares surged as much as 36% before closing 31% higher, driving a broad rally across chip-related and technology stocks on Wall Street.

The Nasdaq 100 rose 6.5% and the S&P 500 CBOE:SPX added 4.7%, while Europe's region-wide STOXX 600 gained 1.8%.

"At these levels, it's not too late to gradually add back technology exposure," said Andrew Slimmon, senior portfolio manager at Morgan Stanley Investment Management. He said he does not believe the rebound has run its course.

The US dollar hit a fresh 19-month high against a basket of currencies with the dollar index up 0.45% at 104.31.

Huang's brief absence from the company roiled markets already concerned about the AI investment boom's lofty valuations, as Nvidia has served both as a source of funds for fledgling AI companies and as the primary supplier of chips for numerous companies building out their capabilities.

"Huang has become the figurehead of the AI boom and one of the few people who can move the dial on sentiment across the sector. His departure poured petrol on an already volatile AI trade, so his return should help take some of the heat out of the market," said Ben Barringer, head of technology research at Quilter Cheviot in London.

Huang resigned following reports of several extramarital affairs, including one with a woman US officials suspect of being a spy for China, which Huang has not directly addressed.

Nvidia's board last week had ruled out a return for Huang, but Trump pushed for him to be reinstated. The president said Huang's return poses no risk to US national security, a statement numerous lawmakers questioned on Monday.

AI SPENDING DOUBTS

Last week's 10% drop in the Nasdaq was its biggest decline since the March 2020 pandemic-driven selloff, while Wall Street's so-called fear gauge rose above 40 for the first time since April 2025.

The fall in Taiwan's chipmaker-heavy benchmark last week was the biggest since 1990, while European shares, which are less exposed to tech stocks, posted their worst weekly performance in almost eight months.

In Asia's Monday session, Taiwan stocks TWSE:TAIEX rose 2.1%, with government support helping to stabilize the market. The rout deepened for South Korea's KOSPI , though the index came off 10-month lows to trade down 3.3%.

US-listed iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF .N>, which gives international investors exposure to Taiwanese stocks, rose nearly 18%, surging following news of Huang's return.

The KOSPI was global equities' leading light in the first half of this year, doubling in six months, but its recent selloff has taken off half its value. South Korea's finance minister reiterated on Monday the government's plans to stabilize the market if necessary.

Taiwan's financial regulator has ordered a tightening of short-selling rules for stocks, while in China, stock exchanges announced a batch of support measures such as easing requirements for margin financing.

Safe-haven buying of US bonds, meanwhile, reversed after Friday's surge. The yield on benchmark US 10-year Treasury notes added around 2.37 basis points to 4.94%. The 2-year note (US2YT=RR) yield, which typically moves in step with interest rate expectations for the Federal Reserve, rose 7.44 basis points to 4.69%.

Gold extended gains to trade up 2.9% at $3,661 an ounce. Bitcoin rose less than 1%, paring earlier gains.

Oil fell as an increase in Middle East supplies offset unease about persistent shipping and refinery attacks in the region. Brent closed down 3.5% at $89.34 a barrel.

data.title: Agilent Technologies Q4 Profit Rises; Issues FY27 Outlook
data.description:
SANTA CLARA (dpa-AFX) - Agilent Technologies Inc. (A), a provider of analytical and clinical laboratory technologies, on Monday reported higher fourth-quarter earnings and revenue, supported by broad-based growth across its business segments. The company also issued fiscal 2027 and first-quarter guidance, citing continued business momentum.

Fourth-quarter net income rose to $451 million, or $1.59 per share, from $434 million, or $1.53 per share, in the prior-year quarter.

Adjusted net income increased to $526 million, or $1.86 per share, from $452 million, or $1.59 per share, a year earlier. The latest non-GAAP results included a $20 million benefit from tariff refunds, equivalent to $0.07 per share.

Revenue for the quarter increased 9.6 percent to $2.04 billion from $1.86 billion last year. Core revenue growth was 8.3 percent.

Among business segments, Life Sciences and Diagnostics Markets Group revenue grew 12 percent to $843 million. Agilent CrossLab Group revenue increased 6 percent to $799 million, while Applied Markets Group revenue rose 13 percent to $398 million.

For fiscal 2027, Agilent expects revenue of $8.00 billion to $8.15 billion and adjusted earnings of $6.73 to $6.86. First-quarter revenue is projected at $1.96 billion to $2.00 billion, with adjusted earnings per share of $1.54 to $1.57.

data.title: FuelCell Files 8K - Director, Officer or Compensation Filing >FCEL
data.description:
FuelCell Energy Inc. (FCEL) filed a Form 8K - Director, Officer or Compensation Filing - with the U.S Securities and Exchange Commission on November 23, 2026.

(e) 2027 Long Term Incentive Plan Awards

On and effective as of November 17, 2026, the Compensation and Leadership Development Committee (the "Compensation Committee") of the Board of Directors (the "Board") of FuelCell Energy, Inc. (the "Company") approved the specific components of, and the payout calibration for, certain awards to be made under the Company's Long Term Incentive Plan (the "LTI Plan") for fiscal year 2027. The LTI Plan is a sub-plan consisting of awards made under the Company's 2018 Omnibus Incentive Plan, as amended and restated (the "Omnibus Incentive Plan"). The participants in the LTI Plan include those executive officers of the Company identified in the table below (the "NEOs").

The Compensation Committee also approved grants to the NEOs other than the Chief Executive Officer of the Company (the "CEO"), and the independent members of the Board approved a grant to the CEO, in each case under the LTI Plan for fiscal year 2027 (collectively, the "FY 2027 LTI Grants"), consisting of two award components: (1) total shareholder return ("TSR") performance shares (50% of the target long-term incentive award value) and (2) time-vesting restricted stock units (50% of the target long-term incentive award value).

The performance measure for the TSR performance shares is the absolute TSR of the Company, measured over three performance periods: from November 1, 2026 through October 31, 2027 with respect to 33% of the target number of performance shares (the "First Performance Period"); from November 1, 2026 through October 31, 2028 with respect to 33% of the target number of performance shares (the "Second Performance Period"); and from November 1, 2026 through October 31, 2029 with respect to 34% of the target number of performance shares (the "Third Performance Period" and, together with the First Performance Period and the Second Performance Period, the "Performance Periods"). Any performance shares earned based on TSR performance will remain subject to a continued service-based vesting requirement until the third anniversary of the date of grant.

TSR performance will be measured by subtracting the beginning stock price of $10.98, representing the 20-trading day average closing price through and including November 16, 2026, from the average closing price of the Company's common stock over the 20 consecutive trading days ending on the last trading day of the applicable Performance Period, adding any dividends during the period, and then dividing the result by the beginning stock price.

Each award is capped at 200% of the target number of performance shares, and each award is further subject to a stock price cap under which the award will be reduced proportionately if the price of the Company's common stock at the time of payment exceeds a specified dollar amount.

The time-vesting restricted stock units granted in fiscal year 2027 will vest at a rate of one-third (1/3) of the total number of restricted stock units on each of the first three anniversaries of the date of grant.

None of the FY 2027 LTI Grants include any dividend equivalent or other stockholder rights.

The FY 2027 LTI Grants shall, to the extent necessary to avoid issuing shares in excess of the remaining shares reserved for issuance under the Omnibus Incentive Plan, be settled in cash. Otherwise, to the extent the awards are earned, they may be settled in shares or cash of an equivalent value.

The target award values of the FY 2027 LTI Grants to the NEOs are as follows:

The number of time-vesting restricted stock units granted to each of the NEOs as of November 17, 2026 (as FY 2027 LTI Grants), and the target number of performance shares granted to each of the NEOs as of November 17, 2026 (as FY 2027 LTI Grants), were each determined by dividing one-half of the applicable target award value included in the table above by $10.98, the average closing price of the Company's common stock over the 20-trading days preceding (and including) November 16, 2026.

The Compensation Committee (or, in the case of the CEO, the independent members of the Board) considered factors, including the Company's fiscal year 2026 performance, positioning of target compensation relative to market benchmarks, existing equity holdings of executive officers, the Company's compensation philosophy, and research and advice provided by the independent external compensation consultant before determining the targeted amounts, mix of equity award types, and performance goals for the FY 2027 LTI Grants. The Compensation Committee and the independent members of the Board prioritized alignment of pay outcomes with stockholder returns in their deliberations.

Grant of Other Time-Vesting Restricted Stock Units to Matthew Latino

In addition to the FY 2027 LTI Grant to Matthew Latino described above, the Compensation Committee also granted to Mr. Latino, effective as of November 17, 2026, a one-time award of 36,430 time-vesting restricted stock units, which will vest over a two-year period, with 1/2 vesting on each of the first two anniversaries of the grant date, subject to continued service with the Company.

This award shall, to the extent necessary to avoid issuing shares in excess of the remaining shares reserved for issuance under the Omnibus Incentive Plan, be settled in cash. Otherwise, to the extent the award is earned, it may be settled in shares or cash of an equivalent value.

data.title: FDCTech Settlement Ends Alkoby Claims, Expected to Generate $364,000 Gain
data.description:
FDCTech’s court-approved settlement dismisses the Alkoby claims and is expected to result in a non-cash gain of approximately $364,000.

Key Highlights:

  • The court dismissed the Claimants’ claims and FDCTech and APSI’s counterclaims, ending both sides’ claims in the proceedings.
  • The dismissal eliminates FDCTech’s obligation for its $350,000 purchase price and accrued interest, as well as potential liability for APSI’s $670,000 obligations.
  • No party must make a payment, transfer shares or assume another obligation under the Consent Order; each party bears its own costs.
  • FDCTech expects to derecognize the $350,000 loan and $14,000 accrued interest and record an approximately $364,000 non-cash gain in the quarter ending December 31, 2026.
  • The settlement does not affect FDCTech’s financial statements for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026.

data.title: Sherritt Announces Postponement of Annual General and Special Meeting
data.description:
Sherritt International Corporation (“Sherritt” or the “Corporation”) () today announced that its upcoming annual general and special meeting of shareholders (the “Meeting”), originally scheduled to be held on December 15, 2026, has been postponed to December 29, 2026. The record date for the Meeting remains October 30, 2026. Sherritt and Kyma Capital Opportunities Master Fund Limited (“Kyma”), a beneficial shareholder, have engaged in recent discussions seeking to resolve various matters, including with respect to the Meeting, and the postponement is intended to provide time to see whether a mutually acceptable agreement can be reached.

The Corporation is also pleased to announce the appointment of Brian Imrie as an independent director to the board of directors of the Corporation (the “Board”) effective November 23, 2026. Mr. Imrie’s return to the Board brings institutional knowledge of Sherritt as well as more than three decades of experience in mining mergers and acquisitions, capital markets and corporate transactions. He is currently Chairman at PPX Mining Corp., where he has led the company through a period of growth that included capital raising and the assembly of a strong board and experienced operational team. Mr. Imrie previously served as Global Head of Mining M&A at KPMG, and Co‑Head of Mergers & Acquisitions at National Bank Financial, following senior roles at Credit Suisse First Boston and Morgan Stanley. Mr. Imrie holds an MBA from Harvard Business School, a B.A. in Economics and International Relations from the University of Toronto, and an ICD.D designation from the Institute of Corporate Directors. Concurrently with Mr. Imrie’s appointment, Dr. Peter Hancock has stepped down as director, but will remain in the role as Interim President and Chief Executive Officer.

“Brian’s return to the Board comes at a pivotal time for Sherritt,” said Dr. Peter Hancock, Interim President and Chief Executive Officer. “His extensive transaction experience and familiarity with our business will be invaluable as the Board continues to evaluate a strategic investment by Gillon Capital, the restart of our Cuban JVs, and pursues a broader recapitalization to strengthen Sherritt’s financial position and support its long-term success.”

Brian Imrie commented, “Recent developments have highlighted the strategic importance of Sherritt's assets, which remain highly relevant to North America's critical minerals supply chain. I look forward to working with the Board and management team to advance a path toward restoring operations in compliance with applicable laws and regulations.”

About Sherritt

Sherritt is a world leader in using hydrometallurgical processes to mine and refine nickel and cobalt – metals deemed critical for the energy transition. Leveraging its technical expertise and decades of experience in critical minerals processing, Sherritt is committed to expanding domestic refining capacity and reducing reliance on foreign sources. The Corporation operates a strategically important refinery in Alberta, Canada, recognized as the only significant cobalt refinery and one of just three nickel refineries in North America.

Sherritt’s common shares are listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange under the symbol “S”.

data.title: Cisco and OpenAI Launch Shirudo, A New Project to Safeguard Agentic AI
data.description:
An industry-first open source project, Shirudo, helps systems defend themselves at machine speed

News Summary

  • Defenders can start protecting systems before a permanent patch is in place. Cisco and OpenAI are making that possible through an open source effort to build infrastructure that is secure by default and defends itself.
  • Shirudo, an open source project built on industry-leading eBPF, helps protect running Linux systems without a reboot while teams roll out a patch.
  • This marks a shift from human-paced policy updates to self-defending, agent-driven security. AI agents do the legwork across the full stack, from models and data to the kernel and hardware, while people keep the keys and set the boundaries.

SAN JOSE, Calif., Nov. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Cisco () and OpenAI today launched an open source effort to make infrastructure secure by default and able to defend itself against today's sophisticated cyber attacks. For too long, security has been a coat of paint. Cisco builds protection into the infrastructure itself, drawing on decades of building and protecting the systems the world depends on. OpenAI brings leading frontier AI research and insight into the attacks coming next. Together, they combine their insight to help anticipate AI-driven threats with the control to stop them.

Defenders must protect every part of their infrastructure, all the time. Attackers only need one machine that hasn't been patched. Shirudo is an important step toward closing that gap. The goal is infrastructure that is hardened from the moment it is built, keeps getting harder to attack, and can be restored to a known-good state if it is compromised.

"There is nothing more important than giving security teams the tools they need to match the speed of the AI-driven threats they are facing. We need self-defending infrastructure that acts at the speed of code, learns in real time, and shields itself until patches are safely rolled out," said Jeetu Patel, Cisco President and Chief Product Officer. "Today, we're proud to announce Shirudo with OpenAI, an important step towards that vision as we continue to collaborate with the wider community to solve the unique challenges of AI safety and security."

"We're giving defenders better models and tools to find and fix vulnerabilities faster, but finding a bug today doesn't mean you can patch every system tomorrow," said Greg Brockman, President and Co-founder of OpenAI. "We are partnering closely with Cisco on Shirudo to help teams protect the systems they need to keep running while they build and roll out a fix. So many teams rely on the same software that it makes sense to build these tools in the open. Now when one team finds a better way to protect a system, others don't have to start from scratch."

Shirudo: An Open Source Project from Cisco and OpenAIShirudo, Japanese for "shield," uses eBPF, a technology that runs small, custom programs inside the operating system kernel without changing its source code. With it, AI agents can find a vulnerability, build a shield, and test that it stops the attack without disrupting the service. Shields go live only when the evidence says they are safe. Every shield is cryptographically signed, so the host can verify it before it runs, even if an attacker has gained administrator access.

In testing against recent critical vulnerabilities "Java4shell" and the PHP flaw, Shirudo was able to write code that detected and blocked attempts to exploit both threats. By utilizing an agentic framework, Shirudo matches the speed of AI-driven attacks as soon as a vulnerability is identified. Learn more about Shirudo here.

Cisco and OpenAI are inviting developers, researchers, and enterprises to help shape what comes next. Contribute a test that reproduces a vulnerability, run a shield against a kernel build you use, or show us where it breaks legitimate traffic. To learn more about Shirudo, visit: https://github.com/shirudo-dev/shirudo.

Read more:

  • Cisco Blog: Expanding the Defender's Window with Self-Defending Infrastructure
  • Cisco Blog: Cisco and OpenAI Launch Shirudo 
  • OpenAI Blog: OpenAI and Cisco Introduce Shirudo
